meta.title: Gmail Video Size Limit: 25 MB Attachments, About 18 MB in Practice (2026) | {{SITE_NAME}}
meta.description: Gmail caps attachments at 25 MB, but encoding overhead means only an 18 MB video reliably fits — larger files switch to a Google Drive link. See how much video fits in 18 MB, then compress yours to fit without uploading it.
og.title: Gmail video size limit: 25 MB on paper, ~18 MB in practice
og.description: Why a 20 MB video still won't attach — and how to get one under the real limit in your browser.
hero.title: Gmail video size limit
hero.lead: Gmail's attachment limit is 25 MB, but the number that matters is about 18 MB: email encodes attachments in a way that adds roughly a third to their size, so a 20 MB video arrives at the limit as 27 MB and bounces. Anything larger is turned into a Google Drive link instead of an attachment.
qa.h2: Gmail attachment limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: Incoming messages are accepted up to 50 MB, so a 25 MB attachment from another provider still arrives.
qa.after: The gap between 25 and 18 is not a Gmail quirk — every email provider has it. Attachments travel as text, which is a third bigger than the file itself, and the limit is checked on the encoded message. If you only remember one number from this page, make it 18.
tool.h2: Get your video under Gmail's real limit
tool.lead: Drop the video below. It is compressed to just under 18 MB on your own device — nothing is uploaded — which leaves room for the encoding overhead and lands the attachment safely under 25 MB. If the clip is too long to fit at a watchable quality, you'll be offered the opening stretch that does fit.
fit.h2: How much video fits in an email?
fit.lead: With 18 MB to work with, length is what decides the picture size. These rows are what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound.
fit.caption: What 18 MB gives you at different video lengths
fit.r1.q: Full HD — hard to tell from the original
fit.r2.q: About half of full HD each way — clear on a phone or laptop
fit.r3.q: Small picture; fine at message size, soft full-screen
fit.r4.q: Thumbnail-sized; watchable, but blocky when enlarged
fit.after: Past about 25 minutes, 18 MB stops being enough for a picture worth watching. For a long video at good quality, a Google Drive link — which Gmail offers automatically for large files — is the right tool; for anything you want as a real attachment, compress it here.
over.p1: When you attach a file over the limit, Gmail uploads it to Google Drive and inserts a link. That works, but the recipient has to click through, the file counts against your Drive storage, and sharing permissions can trip up people outside your organisation. A real attachment lands in their inbox, plays from the message on most phones and needs no permissions — which is why it's worth getting the video under 18 MB when you can.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device and nothing is stored anywhere. Not sure a clip will fit at a decent quality? The bitrate calculator tells you the picture size 18 MB supports for your video's exact length before you start.
faq.q1: Why won't Gmail attach my 20 MB video when the limit is 25 MB?
faq.a1: Because the limit applies to the encoded message, not the file. Email attachments are converted to text, which adds roughly 33%, so a 20 MB file becomes about 27 MB on the wire — over the limit. Files up to about 18 MB fit reliably.
faq.q2: What happens if my video is over the limit?
faq.a2: Gmail uploads it to Google Drive and puts a link in the message instead of attaching it. The recipient downloads it from Drive. This happens automatically when you attach a file over 25 MB.
faq.q3: How long a video can I email with Gmail?
faq.a3: At 18 MB, about two minutes stays clear and sharp, five minutes is fine on a phone, and around 25 minutes is the practical ceiling at a small picture size. Longer than that, use a Drive link or trim the video.
faq.q4: Does the limit apply to the video before or after compression?
faq.a4: To the file you attach — so the compressed one. The tool above compresses to just under 18 MB, checks the result, and compresses a little more if the first pass came out a touch large, so the attachment is never over.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I compress it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only upload that ever happens is the one you make when you attach the finished file to your email.
